newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Deutsche plans full bank in Russia.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Deutsche plans full bank in Russia.

text.p: Germany's biggest bank, Deutsche Bank AG, plans to open a full banking operation in Russia later this year, a senior Deutsche official said on Friday.

Georg Krupp, management board member responsible for Russia, said Deutsche, which was the first Western bank to be licensed to run a representative office in the former Soviet Union 25 years ago, had applied for a general banking licence.
"This year we will convert our representative office into a full bank," he told a news confernce.

Deutsche's investment banking division, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, has been operating in Moscow with an investment banking licence since 1995, but it has concentrated mainly on trading government securities and shares.
"We intend now to expand these activities...to cover all bank activities," Krupp said. "We assume that we can start in the second half of the year after completing the preparations."
Krupp said the aim would be to build up the full range of banking activities, and to do this Deutsche needed to operate in Russia as a commercial bank too.
"Commercial banking is the basis for investment banking, which is our real aim," he said.
In contrast to its strategy in some other West European countries, it does not intend to set up a countrywide network, but will handle all business from Moscow.
"We certainly do not intend to open other branches in Russia," Krupp said.
The bank sees its customers as German companies active in Russia, Deutsche's clients worldwide and major Russian corporations.

Underlining this, Krupp said Deutsche had agreed to lend Russian gas monopoly Gazprom 1.5 billion marks ($887 million) to pay for equipment from German engineering group Mannesmann AG for a pipeline linking the Yamal gas field and Western Europe.
The credit is in addition to a $2.5 billion syndicated loan organised by rival Dresdner Bank AG and signed in Frankfurt on Friday.
Few Western banks have so far set up full operations in Russia, where the banking market is dominated by several large domestic institutions with close links to the political establishment.
But Krupp said Deutsche, which pioneered the resumption of trade between the Soviet Union and Germany during the 1970s detente period, had not been too slow.
"I don't think Deutsche Bank is coming to Russia too late -- we are coming at just the right time."
He said the Russian economy had many problems, but it was clearly on the right path, adding: "We are convinced that the road Russia has set off on is irreversible."
One field where foreign banks, such as CS First Boston, have managed to carve out a strong position for themselves is investment banking, the area targeted by Deutsche. ($ = 1.691 German Marks)
